column1: # Game profile of Castlevania: Belmont's Curse (Switch, base game v0 + update 1.1.0 = v65536, with the Bonus Contents Pack DLC, a licence only).
# Unity 2022.3.62f2 IL2CPP with FMOD, SDK 19.3.16, NVN; subsdk0 is NintendoSDK_movie, which plays the H.264 cinematics. Started from the survey's provisional profile;
# brought up on Android (Legion Y700) on 2026-10-30, not on the Mac or an iPhone
# load order as on Horizon: main, subsdk*, sdk; the RomFS's one NRO is collected and rewritten beside them
# The NPDM declares 16 MB of system resource, so the game has virtual address memory: the 5 GB block of the other Unity games with it (256 MB in front + 4.375 GB alias region
# + 256 MB stack region). nninitStartup hands pool − used to StandardAllocator as one address region, and Unity reserves its own beside it. With the Switch's pool (0xCD500000)
# that region was 3.14 GB and Unity's regions filled the rest: AllocateAddressRegion refused at +4.37 GB of the alias region (4.05 GB reserved, 1.13 GB mapped) and the game
# crashed before its first screen. A 1 GB pool, as Blasphemous 2's: the alias region's high-water mark then stays near +2.5 GB. The sdk build gets the node-area cut (dm/tools/sdk_patches.py)
